prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: N#C[C@@H]1CCCN1C(=O)CNC12CC3CC(CC(O)(C3)C1)C2
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL284

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of human DPP4 expressed in baculovirus expression system using Gly-Pro-AMC substrate incubated or 30 mins by fluorescence based assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of human recombinant DPP4 expressed in baculovirus expression system using Ala-Pro-AMC as substrate by continuous fluorometric assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.72, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 of the same compound against human recombinant DPP4 expressed in the same system (baculovirus), using very similar fluorogenic dipeptide-AMC substrates (Gly-Pro-AMC vs Ala-Pro-AMC) with fluorometric readouts, and both have confidence score 9, so results should agree within 0.3 log units despite the minor substrate difference."}
